pull.title: tracing: run USDT tests without BPF privileges
pull.body:
The USDT functional tests currently use BCC to attach eBPF programs to Bitcoin Core’s tracepoints. This requires BCC, matching kernel headers, and elevated BPF permissions, making the tests awkward to run locally and
requiring a privileged container in CI.

Replace the BCC consumers with GDB. Each tested node runs as a debugger child, allowing the tests to enable the real USDT probes and inspect their arguments when execution reaches the probe location. This continues to test
the parts of the USDT interface provided by Bitcoin Core:

- the probe metadata is present and understood;
- the probes can be enabled and are reached in the expected scenarios; and
- their arguments have the expected values, sizes, and lifetimes.

All five tests can run with GDB and `binutils`, without BCC or matching kernel headers. The ASan CI job no longer needs a privileged container and uses `SYS_PTRACE` instead. This also removes the embedded BPF programs from
the tests, reducing their size and maintenance burden. Overall, the change removes roughly 660 lines of test and CI code.

#### Tradeoffs

- These tests no longer exercise the consumer-side eBPF path, including BCC   compilation, kernel BPF verification and loading, uprobe attachment, BPF-side argument decoding, and perf-buffer delivery. Problems confined to
  those components would no longer be detected here.
- LeakSanitizer is disabled for nodes run under GDB because it cannot operate under `ptrace`. Other sanitizer checks remain enabled.

The remaining coverage is focused on Bitcoin Core’s side of the USDT interface. Testing the general BCC, eBPF, and kernel uprobe is left to those consumers and the kernel.

Concept ACK.

Nice, I didn't know this was possible. I think it's a nice simplification and agree that we should test our interface, and not bcc which might or might not break from time to time. I plan to review this in more detail.

Does this also make the tests work aarch64 ref https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35142#issuecomment-4959156870?
How does this fit into the large picture in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35142  ?

> How does this fit into the large picture in #35142 ?

Sorry meant to reply here sooner but got distracted.

Of course the value to us of this patchset depends somewhat on whether we opt to keep tracing in-repo (vs as an external patchset). If we want to drop it, then this change is moot.

With b10c and the FIBRE team both using tracing actively it seems both would (naturally) prefer to keep it in-tree if possible. This seems fine to me, and I see this patchset as reducing the maintenance burden (to us) of keeping it here in its current form as it:

- removes BCC, root, and host-kernel requirements from functional testing
- preserves the USDT probes and existing production eBPF consumers.

test: Capture USDT probes with GDB

Launch traced nodes as GDB children so the existing probe scenarios can
run without BCC, BPF privileges, or matching host kernel headers.

- Copy probe arguments while stopped and drain complete records in the
  test process, including events emitted during node shutdown and
  restart.
- Follow the bitcoin launcher through exec before registering probes.
- Handle a GDB parser failure for GCC byte-register operands in usdt.py.
- Disable LeakSanitizer only for traced children because it cannot
  operate under ptrace; keep other sanitizer checks remain enabled.

ci: Run tracing tests without BPF dependencies

The USDT tests now launch nodes under GDB, so the ASan job no longer needs
BCC, matching host kernel headers, or a privileged container. Install GDB
and binutils and retain SYS_PTRACE for debugger and sanitizer operation.
Remove the host-kernel package refresh and BCC workflow toggle along with
the dependencies they supported.
